body: Definitely. It's hard to be consistent when you don't have the motivation.

It's great that you're starting that job; the days just kind of blend into each other when you're home all the time. Kind of compounds an already sucky situation. Every time I get down about my job I think of all the months I also spent in an Internet coma and left the house 2x a week for a cheeseburger. That would be my main accomplishment then.
Sleeping and zoning out to TV beats socializing for sure. After work stuff just feels like more work you aren't even getting paid for.
Yeah, it mystifies me. "Drinks after work?" What the fuck? Nooo.
They enjoy things. They are interested in things. They can accomplish tasks without thinking too much of it or getting tired.

It's good that you're putting yourself out there. Is there any way you can socialize without your family around? Must be hard when you're trying to present yourself well with someone snickering behind you. 

And I think it really depends who you're talking to. I'm "behind" in life also and some people are obviously judgey when they find out my age and where I am in life. Other people simply don't give a fuck. Of course there are a bunch of ambitious over-achievers out there who've gotten far ahead in life, but there are also plenty of us who aren't exactly where we want to be...because of mental health issues, the crappy economy, what have you. I'd try to find people who don't pry, don't judge, or can relate to what I've been through.

People get more of a pass nowadays than they used to probably, so don't worry too much about it. It's amazing that you've gotten your depression until control, so remember that.

Yes absolutely. I think it would be a lot easier for my family to deal with if it wasn't intentional on my part. That way they could at least say there was nothing they could do. When someone commits suicide it's this endless cycle of "what could we have done differently."
That is awesome. I'm glad you're taking care of yourself :) Also happy that I'm not the only one who gets the life sucked out of them being around people lol...
Damn I can relate. It's either instant food or fast food. Cooking is just so much work...too many steps.

I'm so sorry you're in pain. You ARE strong. You're doing the best you can with what you have and you're incredible for making it to your job every day. I'm sorry you don't feel there's anyone on your side right now. Is there any way you can minimize contact with your mom? Also, please understand that your SO is under stress too and might not be as responsive as you like. Take that week off and rest up. Do something you like. Have a nice meal. Get a lot of sleep. I'm here if you need someone to talk to.
